chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who goes out on a journey and his wife is with him, can he wash her? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, and (he can wash) his mother and his sister and similar to this, a cloth is cast upon her private part.'
ai.seo_question: Can a husband wash his wife's body if she dies during a journey?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the permissibility of a husband washing his wife’s body during travel, extending the ruling to her mother and sister. It specifies the modesty requirement of covering the *awrah* with a cloth, reflecting the practical jurisprudence of the early Shia community regarding ritual purity (*ghusl*) in domestic and travel contexts.
